title: Repeat Cracking Around the Forward Fuselage Frame Feet Above the Cargo Floor — Request for a Permanent Answer
abstract: Anatolia Skies reports that the same short cracks keep coming back at the frame feet above the forward cargo floor on its older aircraft, and asks for something better than the repeat blend-and-inspect cycle its maintenance organisation is currently living with.

sections.request: We keep finding the same thing in the same place. During heavy checks our people open the forward cargo compartment lining and find short cracks at the bottom of the frames where they sit on the cargo floor beams, usually on the left hand side and usually within a metre of the same station. We blend them out, we do the eddy current check, we sign it off, and three or four years later the aircraft comes back and there is a new one a few centimetres away. On two aircraft we have now blended the same foot three times and we are running out of material to remove. Our engineering manager wants to know whether there is a permanent fix, because at some point the answer to the next finding is going to be a structural repair that grounds the aircraft for a month, and we would rather plan that work than discover it.
sections.background: Twenty-three findings across nine aircraft in the last six years, all in the forward cargo compartment, all at the frame foot to floor beam interface. Two of the aircraft have now had the same location blended three times. The repairs have all been within allowable damage limits so far and none has required Aeralis involvement, but the trend is clearly one way. Our aircraft in this group are the oldest in the fleet and average 14 200 flight cycles. We looked at whether the cargo loading practice is a factor and could not find a correlation with the loading records.
sections.expected_outcome: A reinforcement that can be embodied during a scheduled heavy check and that removes the repeat finding rather than resetting the clock on it, with a clear statement of what happens to a frame foot that has already been blended twice. If a full reinforcement is not possible we would accept an extended inspection interval supported by a substantiation we can show our authority.

type_data.business_justification: Twenty-three repeat findings on nine aircraft, two of which have exhausted most of the blend allowance at the same frame foot. The next finding on those two is expected to require a structural repair with a month of unplanned downtime.
